title: Leytonstone
intro: Alfred Hitchcock's birthplace, with Epping Forest's ponds and woods at the end of the road and the Olympic Park a short ride south.

items.name: Hollow Ponds
items.blurb: Lakes in Epping Forest made from old gravel workings, with rowing boats to hire in summer and woods all around.
items.tip: Boats are usually out on summer weekends.

items.name: Leytonstone station and the Hitchcock mosaics
items.blurb: Seventeen mosaics in the station's subways showing scenes from the life and films of Alfred Hitchcock, who was born in Leytonstone in 1899.
items.tip: Free to see in the station subways.

items.name: Bush Wood
items.blurb: A quiet patch of Epping Forest woodland between Leytonstone and Wanstead, with old trees and an ancient avenue.
items.tip: Walk through to Wanstead for coffee.

items.name: Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park
items.blurb: The 2012 Olympic site, now a park with riverside gardens, wetlands, playgrounds and the London Aquatics Centre.
items.tip: Swim in the Olympic pool: it is open to the public.
